title.narrative: Towards inclusive and resilient urban recovery in Ukraine

description.narrative:
UN-Habitat will support gender-responsive early recovery where-ever and whenever possible, working effectively in the humanitarian – development nexus, while promoting urban and territorial regeneration towards a greener, resilient, healthy and inclusive urban future for towns and cities in Ukraine.
UN-Habitat will have three main areas of focus: 1) concrete urban recovery planning support to 3-5 clusters of hromadas [practice]; 2) supporting the government in improving policies, regulatory frameworks, and instruments to support more sustainable urban recovery activities and prepare the ground for urban and territorial regeneration and more sustainable, inclusive, green and healthy urbanization in the future, while 3) increasing Ukrainian urban planning and design capacity.
Through the development of an Urban Recovery Framework at the national level, UN-Habitat will aim to create an enabling environment for more effective recovery in urban areas. This will help to identify areas for improvement to ensure that national regulatory frameworks, policy and processes support nationally led recovery efforts while enabling bottom-up locally led urban recovery efforts. Housing is one of the areas of improvement, that the Ministry of Restoration has already asked for support. UN-Habitat will strengthen existing approaches and capacities in the country, building on the work of the UN family, the international community at large and national actors, adding value with its urban expertise. UN-Habitat will focus on urban profiling and recovery planning in various locations, targeting small to medium-size towns and cities (<100,000 people) who have more limited capacities and resources, that have either undergone destruction, or that are facing acute service provision pressure due to the high number of displaced persons (or a combination of both). These will be set up to leverage the recovery interventions led by other actors (public or private), increasing their impact. There will be a strong emphasis on the neighbourhood level, enabling also strong community-based participatory approaches. The focus will be on stabilizing populations while improving the quality of life and facilitating returns, when it is chosen based on voluntary, informed consent. UN-Habitat’s interventions are also designed to help decentralisation gains, working closely with all actors and programmes supporting the decentralisation process, in particular USAID, U-Lead and GIZ.
The planning work will feed into the government defined requirements as set out in the amendments of Law #2254 on Regulation of Urban Planning Activities which introduced 3 documents: Comprehensive Plan of Spatial Development, Concept of Integrated Development and Complex renewal programmes, in the medium term. The plans will strive towards high-quality, inspired by the New European Bauhaus, based on good practices of urban and territorial regeneration and urban development in Europe improving the quality and culture of living environment in Ukrainian cities, through emphasis on the cultural context and human-centred designs.
The project activities will fully mobilize Ukrainian planning capacity and ensure cross-learning across all local planning recovery work in Ukraine. The intent is to build longer term Ukrainian planning capacity through on-the-job training, tailored capacity building efforts, and supporting the design of new curricular working closely with Ukrainian centres of education.
